recentItems.title: Iran’s President heads to UNGA as Iran faces new US aviation sanctions
recentItems.description:
Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian has spoken to the media before heading to the UN General Assembly in New York, saying Iran has been at the negotiating table several times and signed agreements, but the world has seen how easily those commitments were violated. He said that if the world wants security and peace, the rights of people and nations must be respected and people cannot be forced into submission through the use of force. Pezeshkian pointed to what he described as crimes in Gaza, Syria, Yemen and Iran, asking whether “innocent school children in Meyaneh” and people in Lamerd were terrorists.
Meanwhile, the US is planning to roll out a new batch of sweeping sanctions on Iranian commercial aviation from Wednesday, with Iranian authorities warning that the measures will affect ordinary people. Mahan Airlines flights to Iraq and Turkiye have been suspended, while other Iranian airlines continue to operate flights to Turkiye for now.

Al Jazeera’s Sinem Koseoglu reports from Tehran.

recentItems.title: HIV clinics in South Africa shrink as US PEPFAR funding is cut
recentItems.description:
Activist Yvette Raphael, living with HIV for more than 20 years, says US cuts to South Africa’s HIV funding were felt “overnight” as mobile and safe‑space clinics closed. PEPFAR and UNAIDS support helped expand testing and treatment and drive down new infections in one of the world’s highest‑prevalence countries. Now programs report staff cuts, fewer tests and longer waits for life‑saving medicines, just as UNAIDS prepares to shut down in 2026. The government says it is trying to fill the gaps, but many worry it will not be enough. 

Al Jazeera's Clement Manyathela reports from Johannesburg.

recentItems.title: UN faces its toughest test under Trump’s attacks in 80 years
recentItems.description:
Each September, world leaders come to the UN to tackle global problems, but the body’s relevance is now under intense scrutiny. Donald Trump’s 2025 “scorched earth” speech and his second‑term record of quitting 66 agencies, withholding dues and bypassing the security council on the war with iran leave the organization looking constrained. 

Al Jazeera’s Rosiland Jordan reports from the United Nations.

recentItems.title: Israel election: What could each outcome mean for Palestinians?
recentItems.description:
Israel's election on 27 October will decide who governs, yet more than 5.5 million Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and Gaza have no vote despite being directly affected by the outcome. Analysts outline three possible scenarios—a Netanyahu-led win, an opposition majority, or a deadlock—each carrying different implications for settlement expansion, the Gaza blockade and prospects for Palestinian statehood. Most opposition figures, like Netanyahu, oppose a two-state solution, meaning any shift is likely to be tactical rather than structural.

Al Jazeera's Nida Ibrahim reports from the occupied West Bank.
